checks.message: New accounts have a root user with no MFA — secure it immediately
checks.context: Every new AWS account gets a root user tied to the email you specified. That root user has no MFA until you set it. Automate baseline security (CloudTrail, Config, GuardDuty, SCPs) via a Landing Zone or account vending pipeline before anyone uses the account.

checks.message: Test SCPs in a non-production OU before attaching to production accounts
checks.context: A misconfigured SCP can lock out all IAM users and roles in every account it's attached to — including your break-glass admin roles. SCPs override IAM policies and cannot be bypassed from within the account.

checks.message: Attaching an SCP to an OU affects every account in it immediately
checks.context: There is no staging or preview for SCP attachment. If the policy denies critical actions (e.g. sts:AssumeRole, iam:PassRole), it can break automation and human access across all member accounts at once.

checks.message: Detaching an SCP removes guardrails from all accounts in the target OU
checks.context: If the SCP was preventing dangerous actions (e.g. disabling CloudTrail, creating public S3 buckets), removing it immediately opens those actions up across all member accounts.

checks.message: Verify the policy is detached from all targets before deleting
checks.context: You can't delete an attached policy, but verify it's not providing critical guardrails before removing it. Deleting a deny-all-regions SCP, for example, immediately allows activity in all regions.

checks.message: Moving an account changes which SCPs apply to it immediately
checks.context: The destination OU's SCPs take effect the moment the account moves. If the destination OU has more permissive SCPs, the account immediately gains access to previously blocked actions.

checks.message: Leaving an organization removes all SCP guardrails and consolidated billing
checks.context: The account immediately loses all SCP protections, AWS Config aggregation, Security Hub integration, and consolidated billing. The root user becomes the only way to access the account until IAM is reconfigured.
